body:
Terminal cloud diagnostics could omit the workload’s already-produced failure examples and lose the entire Prometheus range when a response exceeded 4 MiB. The range also followed collection time instead of the terminal report. This change retains bounded, validated worker/status documents and eight fixed metric partitions anchored to that report, preserving successful partitions and explicitly recording missing or partial evidence.

The collector binds run/generation/snapshot identity, retains raw timestamp precision while using Prometheus millisecond query bounds, and requires a valid failed-before-capacity state before exempting missing capacity documents. The metric partitions share 24 MiB and 60 seconds. Product runtime, zero-loss qualification and cloud lifecycle are unchanged.

Validation includes tests-first implementation, 79 real collector process cases across 20 Python methods, two Go integration entrypoints, and independent Standards/Spec reviews. The initial millisecond-boundary and capacity-state findings were fixed and independently rechecked. Full scripts default tests and the supplementary Mac integration suite passed; the latter used a documented 12-minute local watchdog and does not replace Linux policy.

The first Linux candidate run [39654237841](https://github.com/WuKongIM/WuKongIM/actions/runs/39654237841) passed default tests and migration/messaging E2E, but scripts reached the original 600-second outer limit before completing all cases. No assertion failure was observed; this remains a failed gate. The first [three-node performance/correctness run](https://github.com/WuKongIM/WuKongIM/actions/runs/39654237861) passed separately. All first-run evidence is retained.

A test-only follow-up prepares synthetic SSH response files once per case instead of repeatedly starting Python. It preserves the real collector process boundary, all 20 test-method bodies, every one of the 79 scenarios, and the original test concurrency and deadlines. The first focused follow-up passed both Go entries (retention: 60.60 seconds locally). All 79 complete receipts match the original behavior, with only capture wall-clock timestamps normalized after validating the original file hashes. The next head still needs its first full Linux policy check before merge; local timing is not proof that the 600-second gate has recovered.

The original cloud message-loss cause remains unproven. This PR repairs diagnostic retention and does not claim to repair or waive that verdict. No new cloud run or release is started by this change.
